text:
Anya: Heads-up — proposing an opt-in migration for SDKs to start emitting explicit routing & quota headers for the new platform routing policy. Wanted a quick sync before I open the PR.

Matt: Can you sketch the header shape? is this additive or will it replace current route hint? :thinking_face:

Anya: Additive for now. Plan is to emit X-Redwood-Route and X-Redwood-Quota when SDK opt-in flag enabled. Example:```
X-Redwood-Route: region=us-west;policy=latency;affinity=soft
X-Redwood-Quota: bucket=ingest_v1;unit=tokens
```

Zoe: +1 for additive. We should keep default off so hosted customers don't suddenly change routing. Need docs/console callouts. :thumbsup:

Oliver: How will this affect telemetry tile? the console dashboards expect the old route tags in logs today.

Anya: Console needs a small mapping patch to read route from header -> telemetry.route_hint. We'll also add a new field route_policy in the event schema. Dashboard tile will show policy breakdown once events include that.

Kevin: Any SDK-level behavior differences between Py/TS/Go? polyglot support for header construction might be annoying re: escaping.

Anya: Implementation notes in the plan: SDKs will expose a top-level client option `routeHints` that accepts a small dict/object and serializes safely. For Python: dict -> semicolon-separated; TS/Go will do the same. We will add escaping rules in the spec.

Matt: Need a compatibility shim: servers should ignore unknown keys and we should have a fallback if header missing (current default routing). Also record a sampling flag so telemetry can track opt-in rate.

Zoe: For telemetry I want a boolean field sdk_route_opt_in and sample_rate. That way we can instrument canary adoption. Also add a new eval in Optimize to watch for quality regressions when routing changes.

Anya: Plan: 1) RFC + spec doc today. 2) SDK opts in behind env var REDWOOD_SDK_ROUTE_HINT=1 and client option. 3) Canary rollout: 2% of SDK calls from newer clients for 48h, then 10%, then wide. 4) Console tile updated to show policy and opt-in rate.

Oliver: Tests: end-to-end with dedicated staging cluster, verify fallback if header malformed, and verify telemetry fields present. Who owns the canary gating?

Kevin: I'll own TS/Go client impls. Anya can own Python. Zoe will own telemetry/console changes. Oliver will do runtime tests. Matt will review the spec + rollout plan.

SRE-bot: Canary deployment scheduled: route-optin-canary -> 2028-04-15T02:00Z -> 2% traffic (auto rollback on 5xx > 0.5% / latency +50ms)

Deploy-bot: Note: please add a migration note to the SDK changelog and the hosted API changelog before canary.

Anya: Will open the PRs and RFC today. Quick ask: if we observe route_policy-specific cost spikes, do we have an automatic fallback config?

Matt: Yes — platform will have automatic fallback to default-route when unit-cost > threshold or SLA impacted. We'll include thresholds in the rollout plan.

Zoe: I'll add dashboard alerts for cost-per-policy and token-rate-per-policy. Also setting up an eval to compare generation quality @ 1k prompt samples between default and routed policy.

Anya: Thanks all — will tag people in the RFC and assign tasks. Short-term: doc + safe-defaults + canary gate.

Oliver: :eyes: Please ping when PRs are up so test infra can schedule.

Kevin: one more thing — add a small migration helper in SDKs that logs when header would be emitted (debug) to help users troubleshoot routing surprises.

Anya: Good call. Will add a debug flag and an opt-out note for enterprise private deploys.

Deploy-bot: Canary started (ID: canary-2081-route-01).
